leaders.name: Sarah Chen

traits: patient in 1:1s but blunt in group settings
personality.communication_style: prefers written docs over meetings; reads everything end-to-end; expects a TL;DR in the first 3 lines

decision_style.evidence: data-driven, but values customer quotes too
decision_style.notes: Once a decision is made, treats it as final. Re-litigating is the fastest way to lose trust.

current_priorities: shipping the v2 platform on time (Q3)
improving spec quality across the team
reducing dependency on the founders for product calls
what_they_appreciate: TL;DR + clear ask in the first 3 lines
options laid out with tradeoffs, not a single forced choice
owning a recommendation while staying open to pushback
showing the work — what was considered and rejected
red_flags: proposals that don't acknowledge cost or risk
'we should consider X' without a recommendation
moving goalposts — restating what was already decided

quotes.text: I don't need you to be right. I need you to have a position.
Stop telling me what's hard. Tell me what you're doing about it.
If you can't put a number on it, you don't understand it yet.

feedback_patterns: always asks 'what did you consider and reject?'
warms up when given a clear recommendation, even if she ends up disagreeing
uneasy when a doc doesn't name the cost of doing nothing
consistently rejects proposals that don't include a baseline metric

recent_interactions.what_happened: Read end-to-end, came back with 6 comments. Main concern: I had three options listed but didn't pick one. Said 'this reads like a survey, not a proposal.'
recent_interactions.user_takeaway: Always pick a horse. Even when 60/40, pick. She'd rather argue with a position than evaluate a menu.

recent_interactions.what_happened: She asked what I was doing about it. I said I was 'monitoring.' She paused for 5 seconds, then said 'monitoring isn't doing.'
recent_interactions.user_takeaway: She has zero patience for passive verbs. Bring concrete actions.

recent_interactions.what_happened: I shared early numbers. She replied 'baseline?' — that was the entire message.
recent_interactions.user_takeaway: Never share a metric without its baseline. Ever.

relationship_state.current_standing: good — recently delivered the v1 milestone on schedule
relationship_state.notes: Trust budget is high right now. Good time to push for stretch asks.

leaders.name: David Okonkwo

personality.communication_style: verbal more than written; will skim a doc but talk for an hour about it

decision_style.speed: fast on big calls, slow on details
decision_style.evidence: narrative + signal from customers > internal data
decision_style.process: decides, then sells the team on it
decision_style.notes: If you can't tell him the story in 90 seconds, he'll lose interest. He'll then ask for the doc, but he's already disengaged.

current_priorities: telling a coherent product story to the board
competitive positioning vs. the new entrant
exec hiring (looking for a Head of Design)
what_they_appreciate: a clear narrative arc — setup, conflict, resolution
competitive context, even when it's uncomfortable
owning an opinion confidently, even if it's wrong
red_flags: hedging language ('we might want to consider...')

quotes.text: I don't care about the dashboard. Tell me what changed for the customer.

feedback_patterns: always asks 'what's the story?' before reading details
redirects spreadsheet-heavy reviews to 'who's the customer here?'
rewards confidence — disagrees with confident wrong answers more gently than with hedged correct ones

recent_interactions.what_happened: He asked what I wanted my next 12 months to look like. I had a vague answer. He said 'come back when you have a story.'
recent_interactions.user_takeaway: Even in 1:1s, he wants narrative. 'Story' is his unit of currency.

relationship_state.current_standing: positive but distant — we've only had 4 1:1s
relationship_state.notes: Sarah filters most of my work to him. When he sees something directly, it's high-stakes.
